assumptions.text: 'Customers' means both residential property owners and tenants, and both may submit requests and use the portal.
'Representative' in the stage-management, reminder and resolution paragraphs means the customer service representative assigned to the request.
'Internal notes' are visible only to company employees, never to customers.
The listed stages are the initial status set. The phrase 'such as' and the configurability requirement suggest the list can change.
The online website form is the only intake channel for new requests. The portal is used to track and follow up on existing requests.
All priorities are 'Unstated'. The source uses 'should' throughout and gives no MoSCoW or relative priority, and feedback has not supplied any.
The 5-day escalation timeframe also defines when a request is overdue for managers.
The 5 days are calendar days, measured from the time the request is submitted. 'Unresolved' means the request has not yet reached Resolved.
'Escalate request to a specific escalation team' means the request is assigned to that single designated team, not merely notified to it. This replaces the source's 'escalated to a supervisor'.
Skillset-based assignment is automatic and matches representatives' skills against the request's issue category.

A CSR's 'own cases' are requests assigned to that representative. A maintenance team member's 'own cases' are requests assigned to their maintenance team. 'Other users' means supervisors and managers.
Workload means the number of open requests currently assigned to each representative and each maintenance team, consistent with the assignment window used for resolution time.
Resolution time is defined per assignment period. A request that is reassigned therefore has one resolution-time measurement per assignee.
When a customer rates 1 or 2, the original request ends Closed immediately and the new linked request starts at New and follows normal assignment and escalation rules.

The satisfaction rating is captured when the customer responds to the resolution confirmation request. The rating is also the customer's answer on whether the issue is resolved; there is no separate yes/no confirmation.
'Notifications on portal' means in-portal notifications visible after login. Every customer notification, reminder and message is sent both by email and on the portal.
Because FB-2 states that 1 or 2 means unresolved, a rating of 3, 4 or 5 is treated as a 'satisfactory response' that confirms the request is resolved.
The 6 weeks for auto-close are calendar weeks, measured from the moment the customer sends the satisfactory response. The request stays in Resolved until it is auto-closed.

Answers given in the previous Gate 1 review round are carried forward as confirmed, although they are not in this round's feedback and so cannot be cited by FB id. They are, verbatim from the previous version: escalation timeframe '5 days for all requests'; 'always escalate request to a specific escalation team'; assignment 'based on the skillset of the user'; customer channels 'email and notifications on portal'; customer access 'through portal - autheticated login'; roles 'customer service representative, supervisor, manager, maintenance team member - CSR and MTM can edit only their cases and other users can view/edit any cases'; satisfaction via 'rating'; dissatisfaction handling 'create another request linked to already parent closed request'; 'auto close it after 6 weeks'; resolution time 'open request assigned date / time until it is reassigned to someone else or closed'. The approver should confirm these still stand.

feedback_resolution.resolution: Confirmed that Q-019 and Q-020 are answered. Applied the answers in FB-2 and FB-3, and removed both questions from the open list. No blocking questions or conflicts remain, so readiness is READY. A residual non-blocking gap about customers who do not respond is raised as Q-025. Citations to previous-round feedback ids, which are not present in this round, have been removed. Those answers are recorded verbatim in ASM-019 for the approver to confirm.

Set the satisfaction rating scale to 1 to 5 in REQ-020 and REQ-030, and added a criterion rejecting out-of-range values. REQ-014 now creates a new linked request when the rating is 1 or 2, with a negative criterion for 3 to 5. REQ-013 now records ratings of 3 to 5 as confirmation and 1 or 2 as unresolved. ASM-015 is updated so the rating is also the resolution answer. Added ASM-017: ratings of 3 to 5 count as a satisfactory response.

REQ-031 is rewritten: a request is auto-closed 6 weeks after the customer sends a satisfactory response, with testable criteria that replace all previous <TBC> placeholders. The 6-week value is carried forward from the previous round (ASM-019). Added ASM-018: calendar weeks, measured from the response, with the request staying Resolved meanwhile. The no-response case and early closure or reopening are raised as non-blocking Q-025.

flags.detail: The request form and portal hold personal data (name, email address, phone number, property address) and supporting photos or documents that may show people or private premises. Privacy and retention requirements are not stated (see Q-017).
Client identity mismatch: the project context says 'Reel Estate property developers', while the source says 'We are a property maintenance company' (see Q-018).

A previous-round answer ('create another request linked to already parent closed request', see ASM-019) replaces the source's 'the request should be reopened' with creating a new request linked to the closed parent. This is treated as an authoritative clarification, not a conflict. The approver should confirm the departure is intended.

A previous-round answer ('always escalate request to a specific escalation team', see ASM-019) replaces the source's 'escalated to a supervisor' with escalation to a specific escalation team. This is treated as an authoritative clarification. The team's relationship to the supervisor role is open (Q-021).

Traceability gap. This round's feedback is numbered FB-1 to FB-3 and reuses ids from the previous round, so previous-round answers can no longer be cited by FB id. Citations to them have been removed from source_refs, and their content is recorded verbatim in ASM-019. Values that come from those answers (5 days, escalation team, skillset assignment, email and portal channels, authenticated portal login, the four roles, linked new request, 6 weeks, resolution-time window) now trace to ASM-019, not to a citation. The pipeline should give feedback ids unique numbers across rounds, or carry earlier feedback forward, so the Design agent can trace these values directly.

options: No auto-close without a response; a representative closes it manually
Auto-close a fixed period after confirmation was requested, even with no response
open_questions.question: If the customer never responds to the resolution confirmation request, should the request be auto-closed, and if so after how long? Can a request be reopened or a new linked request be raised during the 6 weeks after a satisfactory response? Can employees close the request manually before the 6 weeks end?

Who belongs to the designated escalation team, and how is its membership maintained? Is it made up of supervisors? Does the original representative keep any involvement after escalation? Does the 5-day timer restart for a request created after dissatisfaction?
For skillset-based assignment: what happens when no representative has a matching skill, or when several do (e.g. workload balancing)? Who maintains representatives' skills?
Can customer service representatives and maintenance team members view (read-only) requests that are not theirs? Is there any administrator role beyond the four named roles?
Must customers log in to submit a request on the website form? How are portal accounts created, for example by self-registration or by invitation after the first request?
Is the listed set of stages complete? What status transitions are allowed, and are any status changes automatic (e.g. to Awaiting Customer Information when information is requested)?
Which form fields are mandatory? Which file types, sizes and number of attachments are permitted? What issue categories exist initially?
Who schedules appointments, and is appointment scheduling itself in scope? The source mentions only a preferred appointment time and a notification when an appointment is scheduled.
Are reminders sent manually by the representative only, or should they also be sent automatically? If automatic, at what interval and how many times?
How should employees match a new request to an existing customer and property (e.g. by email, phone or address)? What happens when a match is uncertain?

Who is allowed to change configuration (categories, statuses, escalation timeframes, notification rules)? What does 'without requiring major redevelopment' mean in practice, e.g. changes by an administrator with no code deployment?
What priority (e.g. MoSCoW) applies to each requirement?
Are there privacy, data retention, accessibility, performance or volume requirements for the website form, the portal, and the personal data and photos collected?

The project context names the client as 'Reel Estate property developers', but the source describes 'a property maintenance company'. Which description is correct, and does the difference affect scope?

summary: The client wants to manage residential property maintenance and repair requests from submission to closure. Customers (property owners and tenants) submit requests through an online website form. They then use an authenticated portal to track progress, respond, upload documents, communicate, and rate the outcome on a 1 to 5 scale, where 1 or 2 means the issue is unresolved. Requests are assigned to customer service representatives by skillset and coordinated with maintenance teams. Requests unresolved after 5 days are escalated to a specific escalation team, and requests are closed automatically 6 weeks after a satisfactory response. Managers need visibility of workload, overdue requests, resolution times and satisfaction ratings, with role-based access, a full interaction history, and configurable categories, statuses, escalation timeframes and notification rules.
